questions.q: According to the polling survey cited, how many Americans think their jobs are meaningless?
a: One quarter
One half
One tenth
Three quarters
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites a YouGov survey in which a quarter of American workers described their jobs as meaningless.

questions.q: Why do pointless jobs persist in the private sector, according to Graeber?
a: A cultural and political bias toward employment
They reliably increase company profits
Government rules require the hiring
Customers demand more personal service
questions.why: Lesson 2 says politicians on both sides push for jobs or tax cuts, keeping inefficient roles in place.

questions.q: What happened when Simon showed a bank software that automated a 25-person team?
a: The executive rejected it because it shrank his team
The bank promoted him and expanded the team
The bank sold the software to a rival
The team adopted it and cut costs
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes an executive protecting his entourage, since losing the team would make him seem less important.

questions.q: How would universal basic income change the balance of power at work?
a: Employees could leave pointless jobs without fear
Employers could pay workers much less
Managers would gain control over tasks
The government would assign people jobs
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues a basic income lets workers walk away from degrading work, so they can choose something meaningful.

questions.q: What does the summary use lottery winners as evidence for?
a: People still want work that gives them purpose
Money does not buy lasting happiness
Luck matters more than effort in careers
Retirement is bad for people's health
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes that winners who no longer need money still feel an urge to work, showing the need for purpose.
